AboutMe.label: About
AboutMe.paragraph1: Maya ES is a German digital fashion designer and a 3D / AI filmmaker. Born into an artist family and trained in fashion and fine art, she found her first true medium in 2019, when she began working with 3D animation. It was then that she recognized the game-changing power of 3D software, becoming one of the first pioneers of digital fashion design.
AboutMe.paragraph2: Her flair for AI storytelling took shape in her work for French couturier Jitrois, whose iconic dress she recreated in CG – designing her own accessories and helmet, and presenting it on Cassie, her own creation and Germany's first CG supermodel, inside a fully CG futuristic world created by her.
AboutMe.paragraph3: The result was a short 3D film, Being a Man: In the far future, a robot – an AI-powered creature – sees Cassie in the Jitrois dress at an exhibition and transforms into a man. Every element beyond the dress itself – the story, virtual world, styling, and film direction – was her own creation. Jitrois published the film, and the collaboration was featured in the Parisian fashion magazine FAUST.
AboutMe.paragraph4: She went on to present her own fashion designs at digital fashion weeks in New York, Paris, and London, and at the Fashion Film Festival Milano. It was there that she recognized something bigger taking shape. AI was no longer the stuff of childhood fantasies - the worlds she'd once imagined through Asimov, Clarke, and Bradbury. At once it was real, an even more powerful, game-changing tool, already redefining culture itself. Once again, she chose to move first.
AboutMe.paragraph5: Today, AI is not optional in cinema, fashion, and music - it's foundational. For Maya ES, that means pairing technical mastery with ethical clarity, treating prompt architecture as a craft in its own right. The result: AI-driven virtual stories told through film, music, or fashion - and, ideally, all three woven into one.

digitalFashionWeek.title: Digital Fashion Week
digitalFashionWeek.storyLabel: Show the story behind Digital Fashion Week
digitalFashionWeek.backText: 3D supermodel avatars of her own creation, staged within fully built 3D universes. Every garment is built entirely on the computer. The process combines pattern-making software, 3D modelling and animation tools, avatar creation software, and numerous intermediate exchange steps between them.

fashionFilmFestivalMilano.title: Fashion Film Festival Milano
fashionFilmFestivalMilano.storyLabel: Show the story behind Fashion Film Festival Milano
fashionFilmFestivalMilano.backText: All the three of her films were selected by the jury and screened in the festival's metaverse section. Set design, costume, and animation were created entirely digitally, using 3D modelling and animation software.

casino.title: Casino Scene
casino.storyLabel: Show the story behind Casino Scene
casino.headline: A room full of bets where nobody wins.
casino.story: The scene is built as a single movement: camera and dress pull the same way while the room tilts against them. The palette stays deliberately down to three tones — the look comes from the grade, not the prompt.

goere.title: Göre
goere.headline: Vertical by decision, not by crop.
goere.story: The frame holds the figure while everything around her falls out of it. The cut follows the snare rather than the plot: every shot ends an eighth too early.

second-skin.title: Second Skin
second-skin.storyLabel: Show the story behind Second Skin
second-skin.headline: Fabric that never agreed to physics.
second-skin.story: A runway without an audience. The garment is simulated in 3D and then generatively overwritten — the actual film happens in between. Cinemascope, because the format forces the body to move sideways.
